• Hence, the correct antonym is** "Common".**

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4'.**

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. I was taking a stroll along the beach, when I came across a heap of plastic waste.

B. Realising the importance of removing the waste, I joined them

C. Some children came to clean the beach, seeing the dumped waste.

D. The adjacent industry had dumped the waste, which was floating, into the water, therefore polluting the sea water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **'Option 4'** that is **'ADCB'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct order to make meaningful paragraph is: **'ADCB'.**
 
• According to the rule of the Rearrangement, the starting sentence should be Introductory.
 
• The next sentence should be related to the topic of the first sentence.
 
• The next sentence is related to the previous sentence.
 
• The last sentence is the concluding sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Pull yourself together
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: '**Calm down'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Pull yourself together"** means to regain control of your emotions, especially in a difficult or stressful situation. (अपने आप को शांत करना)
 
• It is often used to encourage someone who is emotionally upset or in stress to regain control of their emotions.
 
 
• **Example:** *After hearing the bad news, Ram needed a few minutes to **pull himself together.***
 
 
 
• From the above explanation, it is clear that 'Calm down' is the most appropriate meaning of 'Pull yourself together'.​
 
 
• **Example:** *Ramesh took a few deep breaths to calm himself down.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **"Calm down".**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some idioms that convey a similar meaning to "Pull yourself together":

 
 
• **​Take a Chill Pill:** To relax or calm down.​

 
 
• Example: *You need to **take a chill pill**, everything will be okay.*
 
 
 
• **Cool as a Cucumber:** Very calm and composed, especially in stressful situations.
 
 
• Example: *Even though the situation was tense, Virat remained **cool as a cucumber.***
 
 
 
• **Keep Your Cool:** To stay calm and composed.
 
 
• Example: *It's important to **keep your cool **during exams; stressing won't help.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

One is sure ________ what one sees.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**about**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**sure about**" is commonly used to express certainty or confidence regarding something. It is a standard collocation.
 
• Prepositions often follow specific words or phrases due to customary usage, and in this case, "**sure**" tends to be followed by "**about**" when referring to being certain of an idea, fact, or situation.
 
• Other prepositions like "**with**," "**around**," or "**without**" do not form a customary pairing with "**sure**" in this context, making "**about**" the appropriate choice.
 
• Understanding the right prepositional use is crucial for conveying the intended meaning clearly and accurately.

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 1**’.

 

**Complete Sentence**: *One is sure **about**__ what one sees.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "**With**" is often used to indicate having something or being accompanied by someone or something, making it unsuitable for this context.
 
• "**Around**" typically refers to a location or position in relation to something, making it unrelated to the concept of certainty.
 
• "**Without**" means being absent of something, which doesn't fit logically into the sentence structure or meaning aimed at expressing certainty.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He is as concerned as me / regarding / the renewed / examination schedule.

options.text: He is as concerned as me

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**He is as concerned as me**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in this sentence lies in the comparison being made.
 
• When making comparisons, especially with the verb "**to be**," the subjective pronoun form should be used rather than the objective pronoun form.
 
• This is because both subjects are performing the action of the verb (being concerned in this case).
 
• Therefore, "**me**" should be replaced with "**I**" to correctly construct the comparison, making the correct phrase "**He is as concerned as I**."

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 4**’.

**Correct Sentence**: ***He is as concerned as I** regarding the renewed examination schedule.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Segments 1) "**the renewed**," 2) "**examination schedule**," and 3) "**regarding**" do not contain grammatical errors. They are correctly used in the context of the sentence.
 
• "**The renewed**" correctly modifies "examination schedule," indicating that the schedule has been updated or changed.
 
• "**Regarding**" is the correct preposition to introduce the topic of concern, which in this case is the examination schedule.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Ice-cream is liked by her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**She likes ice-cream**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence '**Ice-cream is liked by her.**' is in passive voice.
 
• To convert a sentence to active voice, we identify the **subject, verb**, and **object**.
 
 
• In this case, '**she**' is the **subject**, '**likes**' is the **verb**, and '**ice-cream**' is the **object**.
 
 
 
• The structure of an active voice sentence generally follows the format of **subject-verb-object**.
 
• Only the option '**She likes ice-cream.**' correctly transforms the sentence into active voice without changing the meaning of the original sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2) '**She like to eat ice-cream.**' is incorrect because it changes the verb tense and adds unnecessary detail not present in the original sentence.
 
• Option 3) '**She like ice-cream.**' is grammatically incorrect due to the verb agreement. It should be 'likes' to match the third person singular subject 'She'.
 
• Option 4) '**She loves ice-cream.**' changes the verb from 'likes' to 'loves', which can imply a stronger preference than originally stated, thereby altering the meaning subtlety.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

I said, “They never help anybody”.

options.text: I said they never help anybody.
I said that they never helped anybody.
I said them never helped anybody.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3) I said that they never helped anybody.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech to reported speech, the **tense **usually **shifts back**.
 
• Here, '**never help**' (present simple) changes to '**never helped**' (past simple).
 
• The conjunction '**that**' is often added in reported speech to introduce the clause.
 
• The pronouns and time indicators need to be adjusted in reported speech, but in this sentence, there are no pronouns or time indicators that need adjusting.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is '**I said that they never helped anybody.**'​

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1) '**I said nobody helped them.**' changes the subject and the meaning of the original sentence. It implies the help was directed towards "them", which is not what the original sentence conveyed.
 
• Option 2) '**I said they never help anybody.**' does not properly shift the tense to reflect reported speech, maintaining the present tense instead of changing to past tense.
 
• Option 4) '**I said them never helped anybody.**' is grammatically incorrect and does not follow the correct structure for reported speech. The sentence construction is not proper.
